Method: **50/30/20**. You can change it any time with a tune-up.

## The idea
Split take-home pay into three buckets: about **50% for needs**, **30% for wants** and **20% for savings and debt**. It is simple enough to keep up.

## With your numbers
The paychecks you entered add up to **{{fmt_money(answers.income_items_amount_sum)}}** per pay period. The split applies to each month's take-home pay:

| Bucket | Share | What goes here |
|---|---|---|
| Needs | 50% | Rent or mortgage, utilities, groceries, insurance, minimum debt payments, transport to work |
| Wants | 30% | Dining out, entertainment, shopping, travel, subscriptions |
| Savings & Debt | 20% | Emergency fund, extra debt payments, retirement, sinking funds |

## How to use it
- Each category belongs to one group (see **Categories**). The Budget tab compares each group with its share.
- If needs are above 50% (common in high-cost areas), trim wants before savings.
- Review the split monthly; it is a starting point, not a rule.
Method: **Zero-based**. You can change it any time with a tune-up.

## The idea
Before the month starts, **assign all income to categories** (bills, spending, savings, debt) until *To be assigned* reaches zero. Nothing is left unplanned.

## Why it was suggested
Zero-based budgeting suits irregular income, debt has a high APR, or cash is tight: you only budget money you already have.

## How to use it
1. When income arrives, it lands in **To be assigned** on the Money HQ dashboard.
2. Assign it to categories on the **Budgets** page until To be assigned is 0.
3. Overspent a category? Move money from another category; the budget always balances.
4. With irregular income, **budget last month's income**: hold this month's pay in a "Next month" buffer category.
Method: **Pay yourself first**. You can change it any time with a tune-up.

## The idea
Move savings out **as soon as you are paid** (emergency fund, retirement, goals), then spend what is left without tracking every category.

## Why it was suggested
Your income is stable with room after bills, so an automatic savings rate of 20% or more keeps things simple.

## How to use it
- Set up automatic transfers on payday (see **Recurring**, kind *Savings*).
- Watch two numbers on the dashboard: **Savings rate (3 months)** and **Left to spend**.
- If the savings rate drifts down for three months, the advisor flags it.
Method: **Envelopes**. You can change it any time with a tune-up.

## The idea
Each category is an **envelope** filled from each paycheck. When an envelope is empty, spending in that category stops (or you move money from another envelope).

## How to use it
- Fill envelopes on payday on the **Budgets** page; *To be assigned* shows what is still unallocated.
- Turn on **Rollover** for envelopes that save up (car, gifts, travel) so unspent money carries over.
- Keep a small *Miscellaneous* envelope for surprises instead of raiding savings.
Method: **Track only**. You can change it any time with a tune-up.

## The idea
No limits: **see where your money goes**. Many people track for a month or two before choosing a budgeting method.

## How to use it
- Import or enter transactions and give each one a category.
- Use the **Spending by category** chart and **Monthly cash flow** to spot patterns.
- When you are ready, run a tune-up and switch to 50/30/20 or zero-based.
Where **the next dollar** goes. Work down the list; it is fine to split money between two steps.

items: 1. Budget, plus a starter emergency fund of {{fmt_money(coalesce(answers.emergency_starter, 1000))}}
2. Get the full employer retirement match (it is an instant return)
3. Pay off high-interest debt (roughly 10% APR and above)
4. Build the full emergency fund: {{coalesce(answers.emergency_months, 6)}} months of essential expenses
6. Fund other goals: sinking funds, down payment, education

blocks.md:
## Why this order
- **A starter fund first** keeps a surprise bill from going on a credit card.
- **The match** is free money; skipping it costs more than almost any debt.
- **High-interest debt** is a guaranteed "return" equal to its APR.
- **A full emergency fund** protects everything above it from a job loss.
- **Tax-advantaged accounts** before taxable ones, because taxes compound too.

## Target
Your target is **{{coalesce(answers.emergency_months, 6)}} months** of *essential* expenses: rent or mortgage, utilities, groceries, insurance, minimum payments and transport. It is not a share of income.

| Situation | Typical target |
|---|---|
| Two stable incomes, no dependents | 3 months |
| One income, or dependents | 6 months |
| Irregular, commission or self-employed income | 9–12 months |

## Start small
A **starter fund** of {{fmt_money(coalesce(answers.emergency_starter, 1000))}} (about one month of essentials, or a common $1,000 minimum) comes before paying extra on debt.

## Where to keep it
- A separate, high-yield **savings account**: easy to reach, but not in your daily checking.
- Not invested in stocks: the point is that it is there when markets and jobs are bad at the same time.

## When to use it
Job loss, medical bills, urgent car or home repairs. Predictable costs belong in sinking funds in **Goals**.

## Two ways to pay down debt
Always pay the **minimum on every debt**. Then put every extra dollar on one *target* debt; when it is paid off, roll its payment into the next.

| | Avalanche | Snowball |
|---|---|---|
| Order | Highest APR first | Smallest balance first |
| Interest paid | Least | More |
| Motivation | Slower first win | Quick wins |

You chose **{{if(answers.debt_strategy == "snowball", "snowball", if(answers.debt_strategy == "hybrid", "hybrid", "avalanche"))}}** with **{{fmt_money(coalesce(answers.debt_extra, 0))}}** extra per month. The dashboard shows your estimated debt-free date.

## Good to know
- **Hybrid** clears the two smallest balances first for momentum, then switches to avalanche.
- A balance transfer or refinance helps only when its fees are lower than the interest saved.
- Credit scores typically favour card utilization under about 30% of the limit.

spec.title: Accounts
spec.description: Your bank accounts, cards and loans. Card and loan balances are amounts owed.

properties.name: Balance
properties.description: Opening balance plus transactions; kept up to date by Ultranote.

properties.name: Utilization
properties.formula: if(prop("Credit limit") > 0, prop("Opening balance") / prop("Credit limit"), 0)

properties.name: Aliases
properties.description: Other spellings your bank uses, comma separated.

spec.title: Categories
spec.description: Spending categories grouped by your budgeting method. Essential categories feed the emergency-fund target.

spec.title: Transactions
spec.description: Every inflow (positive) and outflow (negative). Imports dedupe by Import ID.

spec.title: Budgets
spec.description: One row per month and category: what you assigned, what you spent and what is left.

spec.title: Recurring
spec.description: Bills, paychecks and transfers on a schedule. They feed the 90-day forecast and bill reminders.

spec.title: Goals
spec.description: Emergency fund, sinking funds and savings goals. Monthly needed = (target − saved) ÷ months left.

properties.name: Monthly needed
properties.formula: if(empty(prop("Target date")), 0, if(dateBetween(prop("Target date"), today(), "months") <= 0, prop("Target") - prop("Saved"), (prop("Target") - prop("Saved")) / dateBetween(prop("Target date"), today(), "months")))

spec.title: Net worth snapshots
spec.description: A snapshot is taken on the first unlock of each month.

spec.title: Rules
spec.description: Categorisation rules applied to imports, in priority order.
